title: Elucidating the mechanism of dibutyl phthalate on Alzheimer's disease through network toxicology, molecular docking and validation in mouse neuroblastoma cells.
authors: Zi, Jing; Li, Xinlong; Cao, Qianqian; Hu, Yifan; Ran, Zhichang; Li, Yanliu; He, Jiayuan; Wang, Xiaoyu; Cheng, Guo; Xiong, Jingyuan
journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
one_liner_zh: 该文通过网络毒理学、分子对接和细胞实验研究邻苯二甲酸二丁酯对阿尔茨海默病的机制，虽涉及转录因子JUN的分子对接，但核心是毒物-疾病靶点关联，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制研究，方法上仅简单对接，无AI或物理模拟建模。
abstract: Dibutyl phthalate (DBP), a widely used plasticizer, has been suggested to be neurotoxic. We aim to explore possible molecular mechanisms of DBP on Alzheimer's disease (AD) using a combined approach of network toxicology, molecular docking and experimental validations. We retrieved targets of DBP from ChEMBL and STITCH databases, while obtaining AD-related targets from GeneCards and OMIM databases. We identified 193 overlapping targets, and highlighted 13 core targets by protein-protein interaction analysis. Gene ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes analyses revealed that these targets are mainly enriched in neuroinflammation, synaptic signaling, and metabolic pathways. Molecular docking showed strong binding affinities for AD-related proteins, including translocator protein (TSPO), transcription factor c-Jun (JUN), estrogen receptor 1 (ESR1), cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1A (CDKN1A), and prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2). In validation, we exposed DBP (0-200 muM) to N2a mouse neuroblastoma cells for 48 h. Western-blot demonstrated significant upregulation of TSPO, JUN, CDKN1A, and PTGS2, while ESR1 showed an upward trend without statistical significance. In conclusion, DBP may contribute to AD development by affecting AD targets expression (TSPO, JUN, CDKN1A, and PTGS2) and modulating pathways associated with neuroinflammation and synaptic function, providing mechanistic insights on how environmental toxicants may influence neurodegenerative processes.
abstract_zh: 邻苯二甲酸二丁酯（DBP）作为一种广泛使用的增塑剂，已被认为具有神经毒性。我们旨在通过网络毒理学、分子对接和实验验证相结合的方法，探索DBP对阿尔茨海默病（AD）可能的分子机制。我们从ChEMBL和STITCH数据库中检索了DBP的靶点，同时从GeneCards和OMIM数据库中获取了AD相关靶点。我们识别出193个重叠靶点，并通过蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用分析突出了13个核心靶点。基因本体论和京都基因与基因组百科全书分析显示，这些靶点主要富集于神经炎症、突触信号传导和代谢通路中。分子对接显示，DBP与AD相关蛋白（包括转位蛋白（TSPO）、转录因子c-Jun（JUN）、雌激素受体1（ESR1）、细胞周期蛋白依赖性激酶抑制剂1A（CDKN1A）和前列腺素内过氧化物合酶2（PTGS2））具有强结合亲和力。在验证实验中，我们将DBP（0-200 μM）暴露于N2a小鼠神经母细胞瘤细胞48小时。Western-blot结果显示TSPO、JUN、CDKN1A和PTGS2显著上调，而ESR1呈上升趋势但无统计学意义。总之，DBP可能通过影响AD靶点表达（TSPO、JUN、CDKN1A和PTGS2）并调节与神经炎症和突触功能相关的通路，从而促进AD发展，为环境毒物如何影响神经退行性过程提供了机制性见解。
